mainTopic: Whether a סוטה drinks the water a second time (from ״זֹאת״ and ״תּוֹרַת״), then how her מנחה is waved and whether it is offered before or after she drinks.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a dispute in a ברייתא: can a סוטה be made to drink the bitter water a second time? Everyone agrees on two cases. With one husband and one בועל she does not drink again (״זֹאת״). With two husbands and two בועלים she does (״תּוֹרַת״). The תנא קמא, the רבנן בתראי and רבי יהודה each read these two words differently for the two middle cases. רבי יהודה makes it depend only on the number of husbands. Then the chapter היה מביא ends, and a new משנה describes how the מנחת סוטה is waved by the כהן and the woman together, and argues about whether the drinking or the מנחה comes first. The גמרא learns that the owner takes part in the waving from a גזירה שוה of 'יד' 'יד' from שלמים. It then explains that the משנה's list of steps is just the general order of any מנחה. The real timing question is a dispute between the רבנן and רבי שמעון. Finally it quotes the ruling that if she drank first, the מנחה is still valid, and the discussion of that line continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The two cases where everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes saying that with one husband and one בועל she never drinks again (because of ״זֹאת״). It adds that with two husbands and two בועלים everyone agrees she does drink again (because of ״תּוֹרַת״).
steps.simpleTranslation: [She does not drink twice with one husband and one paramour] as it is written, 'This.' With two husbands and two paramours, everyone agrees that the woman drinks again, as it is written, 'the law of.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is marking off the two cases where nobody in the ברייתא argues: the narrowest case (no second drinking) and the widest case (yes, second drinking).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each agreed case is tied to one word in the פסוק. ״זֹאת״ (this) is read as limiting, so it blocks a repeat with the same husband and the same man. ״תּוֹרַת״ (the law of) is read as including, so it allows a repeat when both the husband and the suspected man are new.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This.' A limiting word in the פסוק, used to exclude cases.
'The law of.' A broad word in the פסוק, used to include cases.
She drinks and drinks again (a second time).
The man she is suspected with (paramour).
Everyone agrees (literally, 'the whole world does not argue').

steps.confusionAlert: Here שְׁנֵי אֲנָשִׁים means 'two husbands' (she remarried), not just 'two men.' The suspected men are called בּוֹעֲלִין.

phrases.english: as it is written: "This".
phrases.notes: This ends the point just before it: with one husband and one בועל she does not drink twice. The פסוק is במדבר 5:29.

phrases.english: With two husbands and two paramours —
everyone does not disagree (everyone agrees)
that the woman drinks and drinks again,
as it is written: "the law of".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the point that began just before this section and adds the second agreed case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One husband and one בועל: no second drinking (״זֹאת״). Two husbands and two בועלים: she drinks again (״תּוֹרַת״).

steps.title: The two middle cases where they argue
steps.stepSummary: The dispute is only about the mixed cases: one husband with two different בועלים, or two husbands with the same בועל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is with one husband and two paramours, and with two husbands and one paramour.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the two edges are agreed, the גמרא points to the exact cases where the dispute in the ברייתא actually lives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each middle case has one thing new and one thing the same. Either the husband is the same and the man is new, or the husband is new and the man is the same. That is why the two words of the פסוק can be stretched either way for these cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Where they disagree is...
One husband.
Two husbands (she was married twice).

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פְּלִיגִי בְּאִישׁ אֶחָד וּשְׁנֵי בּוֹעֲלִין,
phrases.english: Where they disagree is with one husband and two paramours,
and with two husbands and one paramour.

steps.triggerLanguage: כי פליגי באיש אחד ושני בועלין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the dispute to the cases left over after the agreed cases of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument is only about the mixed cases (same husband with a new man, or a new husband with the same man).

steps.title: How the תנא קמא reads the two words
steps.stepSummary: For the תנא קמא, ״תּוֹרַת״ includes every case, and ״זֹאת״ excludes only the one-husband, one-בועל case. So in both middle cases she drinks again.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא holds: ״תּוֹרַת״ includes all of them, and ״זֹאת״ excludes only one husband with one paramour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first opinion: the broad word is the main rule, and the limiting word takes out only the smallest case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, ״תּוֹרַת״ is the wide rule that makes her drink again in every case. ״זֹאת״ only cuts out the one case where nothing is new. So both disputed middle cases fall under 'she drinks again.'

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the ברייתא.
To include (to widen the rule).
To exclude (to narrow the rule).
All of them (all the cases).

phrases.english: The first תנא holds:
"the law of" — to include all of them,
"this" — to exclude one husband and one paramour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning of the first side for the middle cases named in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, she drinks again in every case except one husband with one בועל.

steps.title: How the רבנן בתראי read the two words
steps.stepSummary: For the רבנן בתראי, ״זֹאת״ excludes every case, and ״תּוֹרַת״ includes only the two-husbands, two-בועלים case. So in both middle cases she does not drink again.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן בתראי hold: ״זֹאת״ excludes all of them, and ״תּוֹרַת״ includes only two husbands with two paramours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second opinion, which is the mirror image of the first: the limiting word is the main rule, and the broad word adds back only the widest case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן בתראי flip which word is the main rule. ״זֹאת״ blocks a second drinking almost everywhere. ״תּוֹרַת״ allows it only when both the husband and the man are new. So both disputed middle cases fall under 'no second drinking.'

keyTerms.meaning: The later Rabbis (the opinion mentioned later in the ברייתא).
They hold (their opinion is).

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides use the same two words, ״זֹאת״ and ״תּוֹרַת״. They only argue about which word is the main rule. For the תנא קמא she drinks again in the middle cases. For the רבנן בתראי she does not.

phrases.english: And the later Rabbis hold:
"this" — to exclude all of them,
"the law of" — to include two husbands and two paramours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite reading to step 3. Step 5 then adds a third opinion, רבי יהודה's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן בתראי, she drinks again only with two husbands and two בועלים.

steps.title: רבי יהודה splits the four cases two and two
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says ״זֹאת״ excludes the two one-husband cases, and ״תּוֹרַת״ includes the two two-husband cases. So only the number of husbands matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds: ״זֹאת״ excludes two cases and ״תּוֹרַת״ includes two cases. ״זֹאת״ excludes one husband with one בועל, and one husband with two בועלים. ״תּוֹרַת״ includes two husbands with one בועל, and two husbands with two בועלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third opinion, רבי יהודה's. He takes a middle path: the word ״זֹאת״ and the word ״תּוֹרַת״ each cover exactly two of the four cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא let ״תּוֹרַת״ cover three cases, and the רבנן בתראי let ״זֹאת״ cover three cases. רבי יהודה divides them evenly, and the dividing line is the husband. With one husband she never drinks again, whatever the number of בועלים. With two husbands she always drinks again.

keyTerms.meaning: to exclude (to leave a case out of the rule)
to include (to bring a case into the rule)
two (here: two of the cases)
the man suspected of being with the woman

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on the two middle cases. תנא קמא: she drinks again in both. רבנן בתראי: she drinks again in neither. רבי יהודה: it depends on the husband. With one husband she does not drink again, and with two husbands she does.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two middle cases. For רבי יהודה, 'one husband, two בועלים' means no second drinking, but 'two husbands, one בועל' means she drinks again.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds: "This" comes to exclude two cases,
phrases.notes: Both words come from the same פסוק, ״זֹאת תּוֹרַת הַקְּנָאֹת״ (במדבר 5:29).

phrases.english: "The law of" comes to include two cases.
"This" excludes two cases:
one husband and one paramour,
one husband and two paramours.
"The law of" includes two cases:
two husbands and one paramour,
two husbands and two paramours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third opinion, alongside the תנא קמא (step 3) and the רבנן בתראי (step 4).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, a סוטה drinks a second time only when there are two husbands, no matter how many בועלים there are.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter היה מביא
steps.stepSummary: The closing line for the chapter היה מביא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter היה מביא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the standard line said at the end of a chapter. The chapter called היה מביא is now finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It marks that the discussion of the second drinking is over, and a new chapter with a new topic is about to begin.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a chapter)

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter "He would bring"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final opinion in step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter היה מביא is complete.

steps.title: How the סוטה's meal-offering is waved and offered
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה describes the steps of the מנחת סוטה. It moves from the basket to a כלי שרת and into her hand. Then come the waving with the כהן, bringing it near the מזבח, the קמיצה and burning. The rest is eaten by the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would take her מנחה out of the Egyptian basket, put it into a כלי שרת, and place it on her hand. The כהן places his hand under hers and waves it. He waved it and brought it near, took a handful and burned it, and the rest is eaten by the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a משנה. It walks step by step through how the סוטה's flour-offering is handled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new detail here is that the waving is done by both of them together: the offering sits on her hand, and the כהן's hand is underneath. After that, the usual steps of a מנחה follow: הגשה, קמיצה, הקטרה, and the כהנים eat what is left.

keyTerms.meaning: flour-offering
an Egyptian-style basket woven from palm leaves
a holy vessel used in the בית המקדש
waving (the offering back and forth)
bringing the offering near to the מזבח
taking a handful from the flour-offering

steps.whyThisMatters: The detail that her hand holds the offering while the כהן waves it becomes the first question of the גמרא: where do we learn that the owner takes part in the waving?

phrases.english: He would take her meal-offering
out of the Egyptian basket,
and put it into a service vessel,
and place it on her hand,
and the priest places his hand underneath hers and waves it.
He waved it and brought it near,
phrases.notes: "Brought it near" means brought to the corner of the מזבח.

phrases.english: took a handful and burned it,
and the remainder is eaten by the priests.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה נוֹטֵל אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ מִתּוֹךְ כְּפִיפָה מִצְרִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter after the הדרן in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מנחת סוטה is put in a כלי שרת and placed on her hand. The כהן waves it together with her, then brings it near, takes the קמיצה and burns it, and the rest is eaten by the כהנים.

steps.title: Which comes first: the drinking or the meal-offering?
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא says she drinks first and then the מנחה is offered. רבי שמעון says the מנחה is offered first, based on the פסוק ״וְאַחַר יַשְׁקֶה״. If he gave her the water first, it is still valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would make her drink, and afterward offer her מנחה. רבי שמעון says: he offers her מנחה and afterward makes her drink, as it says, "and afterward he shall make the woman drink the water." If he made her drink and afterward offered her מנחה, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a dispute about the order. Does she drink the water before or after her מנחה is offered?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא puts the drinking first. רבי שמעון reads the word ״וְאַחַר״ in the פסוק as showing that the מנחה comes first. Even so, he agrees the order is not critical: if they were done in the other order, it still works after the fact.

keyTerms.meaning: makes her drink (the bitter water)
offers (on the מזבח)
valid (it still counts)

steps.confusionAlert: Even according to רבי שמעון, the wrong order does not ruin anything. ״וְאַחַר״ shows the right way to do it at the start, but the result is still valid after the fact.

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מַשְׁקָהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַקְרִיב אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ.
phrases.english: He would make her drink, and afterward offer her meal-offering.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: מַקְרִיב אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: He offers her meal-offering
and afterward makes her drink, as it is stated:
"And afterward he shall make the woman drink the water."
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:26. Just before these words, the פסוק describes burning the handful of the מנחה.

phrases.aramaic: אִם הִשְׁקָהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקְרִיב אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ — כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.english: If he made her drink and afterward offered her meal-offering, it is valid.
phrases.notes: This is understood as רבי שמעון agreeing that the reversed order still works.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה מַשְׁקָהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַקְרִיב אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה. After describing how the מנחה is offered, it asks when this happens compared to the drinking.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא says she drinks first and then the מנחה is offered. רבי שמעון says the מנחה comes first (from ״וְאַחַר״), but the reversed order is still valid.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר asks for the source of waving the מנחת סוטה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר tells רבי יאשיה not to sit down until he explains how we know the מנחת סוטה needs תנופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said to רבי יאשיה of his generation: Don't sit down until you explain this matter to me. From where do we know that the מנחת סוטה needs waving?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a sharp question from רבי אלעזר: what is the source that the מנחת סוטה needs תנופה? He is setting up the topic for the next few steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the מנחה is waved. רבי אלעזר wants the פסוק behind that, and he speaks very strongly: 'don't even sit down until you answer.'

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Waving an offering back and forth
The barley meal-offering the סוטה brings
Of his generation

phrases.english: Gemara
Rabbi Elazar said to
Rabbi Yoshiya of his generation:
phrases.notes: He means the רבי יאשיה who lived in his own time, not an earlier one with the same name.

phrases.english: Do not sit on your legs
phrases.notes: Literally 'sit on your legs.' He means: don't settle down and rest.

phrases.english: until you explain this matter:
From where do we know that the meal-offering of a sotah
requires waving?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה's description of the מנחה steps
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק source that the מנחת סוטה needs תנופה

steps.title: Why ask? Waving is written openly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders why a source is needed, since 'והניף' is written in the פסוק about the סוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do we need to ask where we know it from? 'And he shall wave' is written about it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי אלעזר's question. The פסוק about the סוטה openly says 'והניף,' so the question seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק already says the מנחה is waved, it makes no sense to ask for a source. This forces us to rethink what רבי אלעזר was really asking.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?
And he shall wave

phrases.english: From where do we know?!
"And he shall wave" is written about it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the question in step 9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק openly says the מנחה is waved, so there is nothing to ask

steps.title: The real question: waving by the owner
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the question was how we know the owner herself must take part in the waving.
steps.simpleTranslation: The question was: how do we know that the owner does the waving?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי אלעזר really meant. Everyone knows the מנחה is waved. He was asking how we know the woman herself must wave it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'והניף' speaks of the כהן waving. The new point is that the owner (בעלים) also takes part, and that needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner of the offering (here, the woman)

phrases.english: With the owner, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 10 by narrowing the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The question was about waving in general
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is about the owner waving

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from שלמים: 'hand' and 'hand'
steps.stepSummary: The source is a גזירה שוה. The word 'יד' appears by the סוטה and also by שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is learned from 'hand' and 'hand' from the peace-offering. Here it is written: 'And the כהן shall take from the woman's hand.' And there it is written: 'His hands shall bring.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יאשיה answers with a גזירה שוה. The same word 'יד' (hand) is used by the סוטה and by שלמים, so we link the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the סוטה the פסוק mentions the כהן taking from the woman's hand. By שלמים the owner's own hands bring the offering for waving. The shared word lets each case teach the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning a law from the same word used in two places
It comes (is learned) from
Peace-offerings
Hand

phrases.english: It is derived from "hand" "hand" from the peace-offering.
It is written here:
"And the priest shall take from the woman's hand,"
and it is written there:
"His hands shall bring."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:30, about the owner bringing his שלמים to be waved.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of 'יד' 'יד' links the סוטה to שלמים

steps.title: Both the כהן and the owner wave together
steps.stepSummary: Each case teaches the other: both need the כהן and the owner. The כהן puts his hand under the owner's hands and waves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as here a כהן waves, so too there a כהן waves. And just as there the owner waves, so too here the owner waves. How is this done? He puts his hand under the owner's hands and waves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what the גזירה שוה teaches. Then it explains how two people can wave one offering together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סוטה teaches שלמים that a כהן waves. שלמים teaches the סוטה that the owner waves. In practice the כהן puts his hand under hers, and they wave together.

keyTerms.meaning: How is this done?
There (in the other case)

steps.whatToRemember: The מנחת סוטה is waved by the כהן and the woman together: his hand goes under hers. This is learned from שלמים through 'יד' 'יד'.

phrases.english: Just as here a priest waves —
so too there a priest waves,
and just as there the owner waves —
so too here the owner waves.
How is this done?
He places his hand beneath the hands of the owner
and waves.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה כָּאן כֹּהֵן אַף לְהַלָּן כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical result of the גזירה שוה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כהן and the owner wave together, with the כהן's hand under the owner's hands

steps.title: How can the מנחה be offered after she drinks if it was already offered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. It asks how the משנה can say the מנחה is offered after she drinks, when it already described the קמיצה and burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: he waved it, brought it near, took a handful, and so on. Then it says: he would make her drink, and afterward offer her מנחה. But it was already offered!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה and points out a clash in its order. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה first lists the waving, bringing near, קמיצה and burning, which means the מנחה was already offered. Then it says she drinks and only afterward the מנחה is offered. That looks like the offering happens twice.

keyTerms.meaning: Brought it near (to the מזבח)
Took a handful (קמיצה)
He already offered it

phrases.english: He waved and brought near, took a handful, etc.
phrases.notes: This is quoting the משנה from step 7.

phrases.english: He would make her drink
and afterward offer her meal-offering.
But he already offered it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the waving source to a question on the משנה's order
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of steps in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already described the offering, so it cannot say the offering comes later, after she drinks

steps.title: The משנה was listing the general order of all meal-offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה's list (waving, bringing near, קמיצה, burning, eating) is just the standard order of any מנחה. It is not a timeline of when things happen compared to the drinking.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: What is the order of meal-offerings? He waves it and brings it near, takes a handful and burns it, and the rest is eaten by the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 14. The משנה's list is simply 'how a מנחה is done,' not 'when it is done compared to the drinking.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 it looked like the משנה contradicted itself. It described the קמיצה and burning first, then said the מנחה is offered after she drinks. The answer is that the first list only gives the inner order of the מנחה's own steps. So it says nothing about timing compared to the השקאה, and the contradiction disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means.' The גמרא is explaining how to read the משנה correctly.
The order of steps for meal-offerings
He waved the מנחה and brought it near to the מזבח
He took a handful (קמיצה) and burned it on the מזבח

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה quoted in step 14. The גמרא is telling us how to read it.

phrases.english: What is the order of meal-offerings?
He waved it and brought it near,
he took a handful and burned it,
and the rest is eaten by the priests.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the קשיא of step 14 by re-reading the משנה's list.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording: the list is a general order of procedure, not a timeline.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say the קמיצה and burning happened before the drinking.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list only gives the internal order of a מנחה's steps, so it does not conflict with offering the מנחה after the drinking.

steps.title: The רבנן and רבי שמעון disagree about whether drinking or the מנחה comes first
steps.stepSummary: Whether the drinking or the מנחה comes first is itself a dispute. The רבנן say she drinks first. רבי שמעון says the מנחה is offered first, based on the פסוק 'ואחר ישקה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the drinking itself, רבי שמעון and the רבנן disagree. The רבנן hold that he makes her drink and then offers her מנחה. רבי שמעון holds that he offers her מנחה and then makes her drink, because the פסוק says, 'and afterward he shall make her drink.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the general list is out of the way, the גמרא explains the real timing question: drinking first or מנחה first. It is a dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן put the השקאה before the מנחה. רבי שמעון reverses it. His source is the פסוק: first comes the burning of the קמיצה, and only then 'ואחר ישקה,' afterward he makes her drink. So the word 'afterward' in the פסוק is the basis for his order.

keyTerms.meaning: Making the סוטה drink the special water
Itself (here: the drinking itself)
They disagree
'And afterward he shall make her drink.' רבי שמעון's source.

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the משנה says 'she drinks and afterward the מנחה is offered.' That is the view of the רבנן, while רבי שמעון holds the opposite order.

phrases.english: And regarding the drinking itself,
Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis disagree.
For the Rabbis hold:

phrases.aramaic: מַשְׁקָהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַקְרִיב אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ,
phrases.english: he makes her drink, and afterward he offers her meal-offering,
and Rabbi Shimon holds:

phrases.aramaic: מַקְרִיב אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַשְׁקָהּ,
phrases.english: he offers her meal-offering, and afterward he makes her drink,
as it is stated: "And afterward he shall make her drink."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְהַשְׁקָאָה גּוּפַהּ פְּלִיגִי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 15 removes the contradiction, this step explains the actual timing question as a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבנן: drinking first, then the מנחה. רבי שמעון: the מנחה first, then drinking, from 'ואחר ישקה'.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list is just the general order of a מנחה. The real question of drinking versus מנחה first is a dispute: the רבנן say drinking first, and רבי שמעון says the מנחה first.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: if she drank first, the מנחה is still valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. Even according to רבי שמעון, if the drinking came before the מנחה, the מנחה is valid. This line opens the next discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: and if he made her drink and afterward offered her מנחה, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new line from the משנה. It is setting up the next discussion about this ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that the מנחה should come first. Still, this line teaches that doing it in the opposite order does not ruin the מנחה. The גמרא quotes it now so it can discuss it, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He made her drink
Valid (the מנחה still counts)

phrases.english: And if he made her drink
phrases.notes: This is the next line of the משנה, said as part of רבי שמעון's view: even he agrees about this case.

phrases.english: and afterward offered her meal-offering,
it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם הִשְׁקָהּ וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקְרִיב אֶת מִנְחָתָהּ כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the dispute in step 16 to the משנה's next ruling, which applies within רבי שמעון's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the drinking was done before the מנחה, the מנחה is still valid.
